fact_en:
Is "we need another test" a real science result?

Yes! It is a real result when your first steps could not decide the final answer.
fact_bis:
Ang "kinahanglan pa ug laing pagsulay" ba tinuod nga resulta?

Oo! Tinuod kana nga resulta kung dili makadesisyon ang imong unang mga lakang sa pagsusi.

findings.note: title_bis "Tinuod nga Resulta: Uli" - Cebuano uli means to GO HOME / return something (Tagalog uli = again is the false friend here), so the title reads "Real Result: Go Home" instead of "Real Result: Retest". Cebuano for another try is usab / laing pagsulay, which the body uses ("kinahanglan pa ug laing pagsulay").

fact_en:
Does a quiet volcano mean it is finished erupting forever?

Nope! A long quiet period doesn't mean it's finished. The next unrest often begins with quakes and extra gas before any ash appears.
fact_bis:
Pasabot ba nga hilom nga bulkan nga humana na niini?

Dili! Ang taas nga hilom nga panahon dili pasabot nga humana na. Kasagaran magsugod ang sunod nga kalihukan sa linog ug dugang gas una pa moabot ang abo.

findings.note: title_bis "Tahom nga Bulkan" = BEAUTIFUL volcano; card is about a QUIET (long-repose) volcano. The card's own body uses the correct word twice ("hilom nga bulkan", "taas nga hilom nga panahon") and the terms list carries "hilom" - the title is the outlier and names a different property than the English "Quiet Volcano Warnings".

fact_en:
Want to test this with your ears?

Just stand still and listen to a passing horn! You will notice the note drop right after it goes by.
fact_bis:
Gusto ka ba mag-test ani gamit ang imong dalunggan?

Barog lang nga hilom ug paminawa ang nag-agi nga sungay! Makita nimo nga moubos ang nota human kini moagi.

findings.note: Vehicle horn is named nowhere in the card: title_bis "Paminaw sa Agianan nga Buryo" (buryo = boredom/irritation) and body "paminawa ang nag-agi nga sungay" (sungay = an ANIMAL's horn/antler). A child is told to stand still and listen to a passing antler, so the activity - listen to a passing vehicle horn - is not recoverable from this card. The card's own terms list has the correct "busina", and 5 other cards in the batch use "busina".

fact_en: A far horn is quieter, but quiet is not low pitch! Doppler is the high-to-low pitch change from motion, not just distance.
fact_bis: Ang layo nga sungay mas hilum, pero ang hilum dili low pitch! Ang Doppler high-to-low nga pag-usab gikan sa lihok, dili lang gilay-on.

findings.note: Body "Ang layo nga sungay mas hilum" uses sungay = animal horn/antler for a distant vehicle horn, and nothing in the card corrects it (title is about pitch, not the source). Reads as "a distant antler is quieter"; correct word is busina, used in 5 other cards of this batch.

fact_en: Hear that church bell across the plaza? It is a perfect longitudinal sound example, traveling through the air all the way from the bell to your ears!
fact_bis: Nadungog nimo ba ang kampana sa simbahan sa plaza? Kini kay pananglitan sa longitudinal nga tunog nga nagbiyahe sa hangin paingon sa imong dalunggan!

findings.note: title_bis "Badya sa Plaza" for title_en "The Bell across the Plaza". Cebuano badya = to mimic/imitate; it is not a bell. The card's own body uses the right word ("Nadungog nimo ba ang kampana sa simbahan sa plaza?") and the terms list carries kampana/batingting, so the title is the outlier. A child scanning titles reads "Mimicry at the Plaza" for a card whose whole point is the church bell as the longitudinal-sound example.

fact_en: Both can be graphed against time! A microphone trace of sound and a bouncing float on a ripple can look like similar wiggles.
fact_bis: Pareho silang pwede i-graph kontra oras! Ang trace sa mikropono sa tingog ug lumba nga naglukso sa balod mahimong susama nga kurba.

findings.note: "Ang trace sa mikropono sa tingog ug lumba nga naglukso sa balod" for "A microphone trace of sound and a bouncing float on a ripple". Cebuano lumba = a race/racing; a float (bobber) is pataw/palutaw. Nothing in the card restores it — title_bis is only "Graph Oras" — so the second half of the card's comparison becomes "a race jumping on the wave" and the child cannot picture the bobbing float whose up-and-down trace is supposed to look like the sound wiggle.

fact_en: One partner can time or run the dipper while the other draws the pattern, so your group observes instead of chasing spilled water!
fact_bis: Usa ka kauban ang nagtakda og oras o nagpadagan sa timba samtang ang usa nag-drawing sa porma, mao nga ang grupo nagtan-aw imbis nga mangdakop sa nagbubo nga tubig!

findings.note: "nagpadagan sa timba" for "run the dipper". Cebuano timba = a pail/bucket; the ripple-tank dipper is the vibrating dipper (kept in English on the sibling cards ffct-36670/36671/36674, and a hand dipper would be kabo/tabo, never timba). The card never corrects it — title_bis is "Kauban Obserba" — so a Cebuano-only child is told one partner runs a bucket in the ripple tank.

fact_en: Want to learn sky knowledge? Ask an elder for permission first, then listen to how their community named stars or warned about eclipses!
fact_bis: Gusto ka ba makakat-on sa sky knowledge? Pangayoa una og permission sa usa ka elder, unya paminawa kung giunsa nila pagngalan ang mga bituon o nagpasidaan bahin sa eclipses!

findings.note: title_bis "Pahina Elder" for title_en "Ask an Elder First". Pahina is not "ask" in Cebuano — it reads as unpaid communal labour (Sp. faena), or as page / pa-hina (make weak); none of those is the card's action. The body proves the intended verb ("Pangayoa una og permission sa usa ka elder") and the terms list has pahintulot/permission, so the title names a different thing and drops the permission step the card exists to teach.

fact_en:
Ever wonder why heavy things don't always win a falling race?

Weight is just gravity's pull! A bigger mass has bigger weight, but that alone doesn't make it land first in free fall.
fact_bis:
Natinggala ka ba nganong dili kanunay nga moana ang mga bug-at sa res sa pagkahulog?

Ang timbang mao ang pag-uyog sa gravity! Mas dako nga mass adunay mas dako nga timbang, pero dili kini nag-inusara nga rason ngano nga una kini mohunong.

findings.note: Definition sentence is false in Cebuano and nothing in the card restores it. EN: "Weight is just gravity's pull!" -> BIS: "Ang timbang mao ang pag-uyog sa gravity!" — uyog = to SHAKE/sway (nag-uyog ang lubi), not to pull (bira/gunit/dani). A child learns "weight is gravity's shaking". The rest of the card is degraded the same way and gives no recovery: the hook question "nganong dili kanunay nga moana ang mga bug-at sa res sa pagkahulog" is unanswerable (moana = to go there, not modaog = to win; "res" is not a word — untranslated "race"), and the payoff "dili kini nag-inusara nga rason ngano nga una kini mohunong" says the heavy object STOPS first, not LANDS first (moabot/mohulog). title_bis "Gibiya-ong Gunit sa Gravity" ("the abandoned grip of gravity") does not repair it either.

fact_en: Weather under Signal 1 can toss light outdoor objects! Bringing in chairs and tying light roofs perfectly matches the described wind.
fact_bis: Sa Signal 1, pwede mapalupad ang gaan nga butang sa gawas! Mao nga dapat itupi ang mga lingkuranan ug itali ang gaan nga atop.

findings.note: The safety action the card depends on is replaced by a different action and never corrected. EN: "Bringing in chairs and tying light roofs" -> BIS: "dapat itupi ang mga lingkuranan ug itali ang gaan nga atop". Cebuano tupi = to cut/trim hair (magpatupi); read as Tagalog it is "fold". Neither is "bring indoors" (isulod / dad-a sa sulod). Folding or trimming a chair does not stop Signal-1 wind from tossing it, so the child gets the wrong protective action; title_bis ("Signal 1 Palipad Butang Bangko") and the rest of the body never say to bring anything inside.

fact_en:
How big is the prostate in science diagrams?

In labeled diagrams, the prostate is drawn as a small gland about the size of a walnut under the bladder!
fact_bis:
Unsa kadako ang prostate sa mga science diagram?

Sa mga diagram nga may label, ang prostate gilarawan ingon gamay nga glandula nga parehas kadako sa walnut ilawom sa pantog!

findings.note: title_bis "Prostate nga Laki Walnut" — laki in Cebuano means MALE (animal), not size (Tagalog false friend: Tag. laki = size). Title reads "prostate that is a male walnut". The card's OWN body uses the correct word: "parehas kadako sa walnut". Corpus check: all 88 other uses of laki in 47,056 cards mean male (laki nga lamok, laki nga peacock, laki o baye); size is kadako/gidak-on (546 hits).

fact_en: Rivers and lakes are freshwater aquatic habitats, while oceans are salty saltwater aquatic habitats for many amazing animals!
fact_bis: Ang mga suba ug lanaw kay freshwater aquatic habitats, samtang ang mga dagat kay saltwater aquatic habitats para sa daghang mananap!

findings.note: title_bis "Tubig Tabang ug Alat" for "Fresh vs Salt Water": fresh water in Cebuano is tab-ang (bland); tabang without the glottal hyphen is the ordinary word for HELP, so the title reads "help water". The batch spells other glottals correctly (pig-ot, tul-id, sip-on, puy-anan, pagpug-on), so this is a real word swap, not house orthography. Aggravating: the body never uses a Cebuano word for fresh/salt at all - it leaves freshwater/saltwater in English - so the title is the only Cebuano the concept gets, and it names the wrong thing. Secondary, same title: alat is the Tagalog form; Cebuano salty is parat/maalat. Low severity (a Cebuano-only reader is confused rather than taught a false fact), but it is the one genuine title defect in the batch.
